{
  "jobspec": "#!/usr/bin/env zsh

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./task2.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --time=00-00:10:00  -> -t 10m
#   --ntasks=1          -> -n 1
#   --cpus-per-task=1   -> -c 1
#   --gres=gpu:1        -> -g 1
#   --output=task2.out  -> -o output=task2.out
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 1 -g 1 -t 10m -o output=task2.out --wrap "zsh $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  shift

  # NOTE: Slurm --partition=instruction not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible GPU resources; you are not forcing the instruction partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mem=20G not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm --job-name=task2 not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  module load nvidia/cuda/11.8.0

  flux run -n 1 -c 1 -g 1 nvcc task2.cu reduce.cu -Xcompiler -O3 -Xcompiler -Wall -Xptxas -O3 -std c++17 -o task2

  values=(1024 2048 4096 8192 16384 32768 65536 131072 262144 524288 1048576 2097152 4194304 8388608 16777216 33554432)

  for val in "${values[@]}"; do
    flux run -n 1 -c 1 -g 1 ./task2 $val 512
  done
fi
"
}
